council.remit_note: Norwich City Council is a district council with city status. Licensing under the Licensing Act 2003 is its job: who may sell alcohol, put on regulated entertainment, or serve hot food and drink late at night. So are bin collections, council housing, parks and planning. Roads and potholes, schools, libraries and social care belong to Norfolk County Council instead, so you will not find those here.

topic.name: Licensing policy
topic.plain_english: The rules Norwich City Council follows when it decides who can sell alcohol, put on live music, films or other entertainment, and serve hot food after 11pm. The policy does not decide individual applications, but it sets out what the council will take into account when it does.

questions.asked: People were asked for their views on a redrafted policy covering alcohol, entertainment and late-night food. The draft adds the 'agent of change' principle, so that developers building next to an existing pub or music venue deal with the noise rather than the venue; it adds commitments on the safety of women and girls and on staff getting home after late shifts, and it would let the council restrict sales of very strong alcohol at off-licences where there is evidence of street drinking. Sixty-seven responses came in before the consultation closed on 9 August 2026. What people actually said has not been published.
questions.decided: One decision so far. On 5 March 2026 the Licensing committee went through the draft, changed the wording on licence conditions, asked officers to look again at signage and at logbook inspections, and recommended that Cabinet put the draft out to public consultation. We could not find a published Cabinet decision agreeing that, even though the consultation went ahead. The meeting where the responses are due, on 17 September 2026, had no papers published as of 7 September.
questions.done: Nothing yet. The policy Norwich actually applies today is still the one full council approved in December 2021, and it stays in force until a revised policy is adopted. Officers proposed taking a final version to full council in November 2026 so it could start on 1 December 2026. Until that happens, we are still waiting.
